title: Browser Exit Drill
oneLiner: 종료 전 브라우저의 탭·스페이스·확장·권한보다 실제 업무 한 건을 새 브라우저에서 재현해 무엇이 끊기는지 확인하는 이사 훈련.
theme: unclassified — continuity of a personal work habitat.
targetUser: Arc users, browser-dependent freelancers, research teams, customer-support teams, and IT administrators.
keyUX: select task → old-browser step chain → candidate mapping → permission/extension blockers → timed replay → compare → choose, postpone, or keep split-browser.

sourceSignals.note: Arc shutdown creates a fixed browser migration deadline.

23,855 stars in about 5.62 days showed that users trust disruptive device changes more when the after-state and restore path are visible; p006 transfers that lesson to browser migration rather than TV cleanup.

whyStarred: 23,855 stars in about 5.62 days showed that users trust disruptive device changes more when the after-state and restore path are visible; p006 transfers that lesson to browser migration rather than TV cleanup.
mechanic: choose one recurring task, capture its old-browser path, preview import/restore, then complete the task in the candidate browser under the same checkpoints.
triggerMoment: a shutdown or account-sync deadline is announced.
buyerShareAudience: individuals, team leads, browser vendors, and migration consultants.
userActionSentence: “북마크 말고, 월요일 아침에 하던 일이 그대로 되는지 확인하고 싶어요.”
threeSecondSting: “12/22까지 60일 · 북마크 완료 · 실제 업무 0/3 검증” exposes the false sense of completion.
outputArtifact: browser exit passport with verified tasks, unresolved blockers, fallback, and retest date.
firstValidationTest: migrate three real tasks for ten Arc users and measure hidden blockers found before switching.
lovedBySmallGroup: 4/5 — freelancers and small teams with browser-specific research, publishing, support, or sales routines face a fixed cutoff.
smallGroupFit: teams with three to ten browser-critical workflows can finish a meaningful drill before enterprise migration tooling would be justified.
spreadTrigger: a task-level exit card shows coworkers exactly which blocker remains and which browser is ready.
referencePattern: evacuation drill + cross-browser test harness + reversible device-change preview.
twist: success is completing a real job, not reaching 100% imported items.
firstScreen: fixed shutdown date, three recurring tasks, and the mismatch “data exported / work unverified”.
shareOrPlayLoop: capture task → preview change → replay in candidate → record blocker → fix/retest → share passport.
planBrief: User problem: export counts hide behavior loss. Inflow: shutdown notice. Business: individual paid pack or team migration report. Core loop: task select → old path → map → replay → compare → fallback. First screen: deadline and unverified tasks. Rules: no claim of full migration; every blocker ties to a step; preserve old browser until user signs off. QA: missing extension, OAuth popup, keyboard shortcut conflict, local-only data, failed import, two-browser fallback, reduced motion. Risk: prototype mocks browser integrations.
developmentStartPrompt: Build a cross-browser migration workbench with a fixed cutoff, three mocked recurring tasks, old/new step chains, extension and permission blockers, import preview, restore path, timed replay, side-by-side outcome, split-browser fallback, and exportable exit passport.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive global migration workbench called “Browser Exit Drill” for Arc users and small teams facing the 2026-12-22 shutdown. Open with a fixed deadline and an uncomfortable mismatch: “Bookmarks exported · real work verified 0/3.” Let the user choose one recurring job—research and publish a client brief—then show the exact old-browser chain of spaces, pinned tabs, keyboard shortcuts, extensions, permissions, and sign-ins. Preview what the candidate browser can import, keep a visible restore/keep-Arc path, and make the user complete the same job in a timed replay. Surface a missing extension, blocked OAuth popup, shortcut collision, and local-only note; compare outcome and effort, then choose ready, split-browser fallback, or retest. Required sections: cutoff, task picker, old path, candidate mapping, gaps, preview/restore, replay, comparison, fallback, and exit passport. Emotional pressure: losing a work habitat while believing an export file is enough. Design direction: use the financial-analyst profile with cool off-white, ink, one cobalt action accent, precise side-by-side lanes, tabular dates and durations, written interpretation beside each number, disciplined 8px radii, and no generic migration progress dashboard.
